Justin Blond –Bike control on 1st Avenue. Looking for help and assistance on the bike corral on 1st avenue and 11th street. Family owns a building there. Situation has become dire. No room to walk on the sidewalk. 400 bikes parked at all times. Retail stores cannot stay in business. It’s very hard, in under 2 years 4 tenants go out, property taxes going up, we are at risk of losing the building. It’s a tough time. Most people don’t care about the small landlord, we are regular people looking for help. Unmanageable with rats, very poorly kept and difficult people coming out of the hallways and people being harassed. It’s not a good situation and not what I know and love about this city. If there is any assistance and ideas. It’s a very bad situation at this point.

11th Street bike corrals. I’m also here to speak about the bike corral. All the storefront on that block from the corner to 11th streets, 6-7 of them, they’re either closed or cannot pay their rent because of what’s going on. We have been speaking to you guys for a couple of years now. How I this a normal thing, It’s become a parking lot, why isn’t there one Infront of a school or Tompkins square park. But those are all small business. No chipotle or sweet greens. All people have gone out of business. Residential tenants trouble getting gin out and out because people sit on stoop. It’s several years and has only gotten worse and worse. Nobody responds to anything. They sway we are looking at it thinking about it talking about, but it’s only gotten worse. Bangladeshi deli there 22 years are 7months behind on rent. He was going to come down here. He is about to go out of business also. He’s the last retail tenant of 9 storefronts that er impacted by these bikes that block foot traffic . how many people must lose their jobs before we care?

speaker_line: Gavin Marcus from ABC No Rio
text: Volunteer led community center for Art and DIY center will back around 10/2026. Since 1980 volunteer led community center for art and DIY culture. We are at 156 Rivington. We have been in exile for 15 years. We are artist and activists that should be accessible to everyone and share resources. When the building opens, 10 year absence, made way for construction project of 2-3 years we are now 10 years but 3 months to completing our community center and hope end of October to open. Inclusive DIY space for artists and the neighborhood community. Low cost dark room, computer lab, zine library, performance space for art, gallery for art exhibitions, public events, concerts, still very much intertwined. At the same time we want to acknowledge from 10 year absence we want to open up conversation the engage community we left and talk about resources and communities and program we run and how we can best offer programs and services that benefit everyone. Get in touch.
